With belt pass-through each motor holds the motor-side torque C^-T tau, not the joint torque (see mass_props.json motor_map).
Budget = holding torque x ratio x 50% (standards rule 4). Holding torque is assumed until the motor model is confirmed.

decisions.text: Correct requirements to 600 g and gate new CAD on capacity screening and user concept selection (why: explicit payload answer supersedes 100 g; existing performance is not verified at 600 g).

Add an independent Uno built-in LED blink test using board id uno; default to 1 second on/off and a serial heartbeat (why: the user explicitly requests a board test, independent of the arm firmware handled by their friend).

Supersede queued demo tasks T101-T104 and blocked T108 with T111 inventory completion, T112 missing prior art and T113 concept selection (why: baseline T105 is absent, T106 lacks a completion summary, and 600 g screening fails; no heavy CAD before selection).
Schedule T110 to recheck the connected Uno and restore the existing blink only if needed (why: the new inbox request postdates the completed T109 test; reuse its verified defaults).

open_decisions.text: the 4th motor/driver — vendor rail module or a wrist servo (spare).

Choose a concept to develop for the 600 g arm. A is the conventional first option; A and B are the proposed CAD/simulation comparison pair, with C available if you prefer counterweights. No new CAD until your pick. All retain four owned motors, wrist roll, MG90S, black finish, X1E fit target and PETG exceptions. Grip, exact motor/step-rate capability and delivered cost below $100 remain unverified; choosing a concept does not approve fabrication or a budget increase.

not_verified.text: belt tensioning and tooth skipping, printed-surface quality, joint stiffness/backlash, infill-based masses (estimate — weigh the parts), home sensor positions (estimates, calibrate). Open decisions: the 4th motor/driver — vendor rail module or a wrist servo (spare).
